title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page axiomatizes an 'elementary divided-power (PD) de Rham algebra' K^{••}. It serves as a local, linear model for the PD de Rham complex of a PD envelope, the object studied in the preceding pages (immersions u: Z → 𝔓 and the complexes K_u^{••}).

Axioms:
(a) K is a bigraded ring K^{ij} with i, j ≥ 0. It is graded-commutative (alternating) for the 'exterior degree' j.
(b) The augmentation ideal ⊕_{i+j>0} K^{ij} carries a PD structure.
(c) There is a differential d, a derivation for the exterior grading with signs taken from the total degree, compatible with the divided powers.
(d) d: K^{1,0} = Φ → K^{1,1} = Ψ is an epimorphism. The machine transcription reads 'isom', but the image and the sequel ('L = Ker d') require 'ép(i)'.
(e) With k = K^{00}, K is the free alternating PD algebra on Φ (bidegree (1,0)) and Ψ (bidegree (1,1)). That is, K ≅ Γ_k(Φ) ⊗ Λ_k(Ψ), whose weight-n part is Γ^{n-j}Φ ⊗ Λ^jΨ in exterior degree j. Hence K^{ij} = 0 for j > i.
(f) Φ and Ψ are k-flat, so L = Ker(d: Φ → Ψ) is flat. This is the weight-1, exterior-degree-0 cohomology of K.

Consequence: H^{*i}(K) = Γ^*L for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0. In each weight n, the complex Γ^nΦ → Γ^{n-1}Φ⊗Ψ → … → Λ^nΨ is the divided-power Koszul complex attached to the flat short exact sequence 0 → L → Φ → Ψ → 0. It is acyclic except in degree 0, where it gives Γ^nL. So K is a PD-dg resolution of the PD algebra Γ_k(L).

(g) From now on L is mostly assumed locally free of rank 1, with variants 'free of rank 1' and 'trivialized'. Then Γ^*L is locally the PD polynomial algebra in one variable, i.e. the PD envelope of the origin on a line.

In modern terms, Γ_k(L) for L invertible is the coordinate ring of a divided-power line, and K is the PD de Rham complex of the PD polynomial algebra Γ(Φ) with Ω^1 = Ψ, killing exactly the directions in Ψ. This is a model for the 'PD Poincaré lemma relative to a sub-line', a building block for comparing PD de Rham complexes of different embeddings and, plausibly, for crystalline Chern-class or rank-one computations.
errors: The machine transcription of (d) as 'est un isom.' is inconsistent with the rest. If d: Φ → Ψ were an isomorphism, L = Ker d = 0 and the claimed cohomology Γ^*L would be just k. The image reads 'ép.' (epimorphism), which makes everything correct.

Exactness of the PD Koszul complex in all characteristics needs the flatness assumption (f) and the surjectivity in (d). With those it is standard (cf. Illusie, Complexe cotangent I, Koszul complexes for Γ and Λ). No genuine gap.
Notation H^{*i} and 'H^1(K)' for L is loose: L is the weight-1, exterior-degree-0 cohomology.

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of a bigraded alternating PD-dg algebra ('algèbre de DR à p.d. élémentaire') free on Φ in bidegree (1,0) and Ψ in bidegree (1,1)
ideas.modern_name: PD de Rham complex of a divided-power polynomial algebra / PD Koszul dg-algebra
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known; the 1976 IHÉS talk was not published (unsure about circulated notes)

ideas.what: Γ(Φ)⊗Λ(Ψ) with d induced by an epi Φ → Ψ of flat modules resolves Γ(Ker)
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power Koszul resolution / PD Poincaré lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie, Berthelot (Koszul complexes for Γ, Λ, S in Complexe cotangent; PD Poincaré lemma in crystalline cohomology)

ideas.what: Restriction to L locally free of rank 1 (PD line), with variants free and trivialized
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power line / PD-hull of a line bundle (cf. G_a^♯)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Berthelot); G_a^♯ prominent in Drinfeld and Bhatt–Lurie prismatization

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates an abstract 'elementary PD de Rham algebra' as a structure (bigraded PD-dg algebra resolving Γ(L) for an invertible L), apparently intending to classify or rigidify such objects, as in the functoriality discussion of the previous page. This axiomatic packaging, as opposed to the concrete PD envelope, is not a standard notion in the literature. It is a mild documentary point about the content of the unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: K^{••} Algèbre de DR à p.d. élémentaire ... K^{••} est une résolution de Γ^*L. On va supposer le plus souvent g) L est un k-Module loc. libre de rang 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rank-one PD algebras Γ(L) and their de Rham resolutions are the coordinate-ring level of G_a^♯-type objects central to prismatization and Cartier–Witt stacks. The page documents Grothendieck working with this structure in 1975-76, but it contains no result beyond standard facts.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean axiomatization of the PD de Rham/Koszul algebra and a standard exactness consequence. Its interest is mainly historical, as evidence of the content of the unpublished 1976 IHÉS talk, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: (d) should read 'd: K^{1,0} = Φ → K^{11} = Ψ est un ép[imorphisme]', not 'est un isom.'
In (f), L = Ker d is the cohomology in weight 1 and exterior degree 0 (written roughly as H^{1·} or H^{1,0}(K^{••}) in the image), not 'H^1'.
(e): the inserted word above 'à p.d.' is 'alternée' (free alternating PD algebra).
